fields: He is a tank, so pulling him into your team rarely pays off and usually just hands him an engage.
A tank you should not pull: a grab gives him a chance to all-in with his ult, or he can simply W back to an ally.
Her Black Shield blocks your hook and undermines your whole game plan.
A favorable lane; land a hook and he is easy to burst.
A skill matchup where whoever lands first usually wins. You can interrupt his shield or W dash, but if his knockup lands first you rarely trade back in time.
A ranged support with no mobility; a landed hook usually means a kill.
Immobile and ranged, but her plants can block your hook, so aim around them.
While his blink is available your hook is effectively useless against him, so wait for it to be on cooldown.
A ranged support with a bit more mobility, and she can knock you away with her ult right after you hook her.
He is very mobile and hard to hook in open lane, so only target him when his cooldowns are down. If you land the hook, use E immediately to cancel his dash.
A mobile ranged support who can poke you down heavily if you play loose.
Another tank you should avoid pulling into your own team.
She cannot defend herself well in lane but becomes a real threat later, so punish her early.
A tank you do not want to hook into your team.
Immobile, so hooking her is usually enough to win the exchange.
Rarely played, and the author sees him as no real concern.
Think very carefully before hooking him, since pulling him in can backfire.
The author considers him weak and rarely seen, so he is not much of a threat.
Catching her while detached usually wins the lane, but she becomes a major late-game threat if left alone.
If your team cannot burst him right after the hook, he will land his full combo on you.
